sections.overview: Rhopalura ophiocomae is a parasitic orthonectid associated with brittle stars.
sections.identification: It is a microscopic member of the genus Rhopalura; orthonectids are recognized by specialized cellular and reproductive anatomy.
sections.habitat: Records are from marine ophiuroids, including the brittle star Amphipholis squamata.
sections.diet: It parasitizes its host rather than feeding as a free-living animal; plasmodia develop in the host’s body cavity and reproductive tissues.
sections.behavior: Adult stages leave the host and enter seawater, where reproduction takes place.
sections.reproduction: Males and females are separate; fertilized eggs develop into ciliated larvae that seek a new host.
sections.ecology: Its documented host differs from that of R. granosa, which was described from the bivalve Heteranomia squamula.
sections.conservation: The cited studies describe host biology rather than conservation status.
